reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal behavior exhibits a robust ~91-point periodicity (confirmed by metadata), with three to five full cycles visible per reference. Each cycle contains a characteristic asymmetric waveform: a relatively sharp, narrow peak (duration ~5–8 points) followed by a broader, gently sloping trough (~15–20 points) before the next rise. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is consistently ~2.3–2.7 robust-standardized units, with median levels varying modestly across segments (−0.34 to +0.32), indicating baseline shifts but no persistent trend. Roughness (~0.337) and curvature (~0.337–0.670) are tightly clustered, reflecting stable local dynamics. Noise is low-to-moderate, appearing as fine-grained jitter superimposed on the main motif; no sustained high-frequency bursts or flatlining occur in consensus regions. Peaks are typically sharp and unimodal; troughs may show minor plateaus but not prolonged saturation. Boundary truncation is minimal—each segment starts/ends mid-cycle without artificial cutoffs. Acceptable variation includes small baseline offsets, slight cycle stretching/compression (<±5% in period), and occasional minor secondary inflections near peak shoulders, but not deep secondary minima or abrupt level jumps within a cycle.

Reference 1 should be used only when a mild negative trend is observed in the query, and its anomalous spike must be treated as non-representative.
